newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight ends up amid volatile swaps.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight ends up amid volatile swaps.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate ended slightly higher after fluctuating due to a volatile swaps market, dealers said on Friday.
They said the wild movement in swaps, triggered by rumours of a Bank Negara meeting with bank chief executives, dictated the trend in the interbank money market for most of the day.
The maturity of a 500 million ringgit Bank Negara bill issue also helped keep the overnight down, they said.
The overnight rate ended at 5.8/9 percent against 5.5 after moving between 5.5 and 6.0 percent.
The dealers said there were also rumours that foreigners have been borrowing ringgit since Thursday morning through swaps, which have risen sharply.
"Swaps came off in between and then went up again," said a dealer with a large Malaysian bank.
He said the swaps came off probably on unwinding of long ringgit positions by speculators who fear that Bank Negara may pre-empt their plans of hitting on the ringgit.

Dealers said there were also talk that the rumoured Bank Negara meeting on Saturday with chief executives of Malaysian banks would discuss the possibility of introducing selective capital controls to defend the ringgit.
The ringgit has been under speculative attack in the wake of a crisis in the Thai baht, which has been floated since Wednesday.
The central bank could not be reached for comment. It also does not usually comment on its open market operations.

The rumours have sent swaps soaring since Thursday, with one-month swaps up at 100 points from 17 and six-month at 270/300 from 160. They fell to around 50 and 200 mid-session before recovering to around 75/80 and 270/90.
Earlier, other interbank rates were firmer after the surge in swap points, dealers said.
"Swaps have moved a lot to the right and this is pushing interbank rates higher," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank. "But I don't think rates can go much higher as the market is still flush."
One-week money was at 7.00/50 percent against 6.40/50 on Thursday.
One-month money was at 7.50/60 percent from 7.25 percent, and three-month was also at 7.50/60 percent against 7.35/40.
The dealers said there will be some tightness next week due to a one-billion ringgit bill issue.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were mostly lower due to the surge in swaps.
"The near months fell because of the movement in swaps," said a futures dealer with a Malaysian bank.
At the close, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was down three at 92.55, or an implied yield of 7.45 percent.
The December contract was down three at 92.70, or 7.30 percent and March 1998 was unchanged at 92.74, or 7.26 percent.
-- Madhav Reddy (603-201 4813) .
